archetype.name: Pocket Passer (vertical)
archetype.definition: A rhythm thrower who almost never leaves the pocket (one scramble in 197 dropbacks) and makes his money pushing the ball 20-plus yards downfield, at his best off under-center play-action rather than straight dropback football.

report.headline: Shaky accuracy masked by deep shots, but the arrow is pointing up
report.take:
Love's 2026 line looks like a top-five passer's at first glance: third in yards, fifth in touchdowns. Underneath it is a quarterback who has been less accurate than the throws he's attempting. His CPOE of -2.05 ranks 32nd of 43, and his bad-throw rate of 18.4% is 35th of 36. That is a sharp break from 2025, when he was eighth in CPOE (+5.5), 14th in bad-throw rate (12.5%) and fifth in EPA per play. The yardage total is also inflated by script. He threw 42 times in a 39-22 loss at Minnesota and 53 times in a 35-14 home loss to Atlanta. He finished both of those games with large yardage totals while posting -2.7 and +3.6 passing EPA.

What is carrying the efficiency is the vertical game and the under-center package. On 27 throws of 20-plus air yards he has +0.714 EPA per attempt and a +7.4 CPOE, with Christian Watson producing +0.507 EPA per target. Under center he is +0.455 EPA per play with a +13.3 CPOE. Out of shotgun he is basically break-even at +0.013. LaFleur's offense works when the run threat and play-action move linebackers. The problem is that the actual run game is dead last in EPA at -0.333 per carry.

That broken run game is the root of his worst number. On third down he faces an average of 8.2 yards to go and converts only 27.5%, at -0.205 EPA per play. The line is also allowing hits at the third-worst rate in the league. Long-yardage, obvious-passing-down football out of shotgun is exactly where his accuracy has slipped. Some of that is on him, but much of it is the situation.

The last two weeks look much more like the 2025 version. He posted +5.3 and +16.2 CPOE against Tampa and Chicago, and the 31-7 Bears win (25 of 31, 367 yards, +16.9 EPA) was his cleanest game of the year. The Week 1 meltdown came with a 47.8% pressure rate against what is now the league's top-ranked defense. With a three-year track record of being an accurate, efficient starter, the bet is that the CPOE climbs back toward neutral rather than staying in the bottom quarter.

strengths.title: Deep ball is a real weapon
strengths.body: His 20-plus air-yard throws are producing +0.714 EPA each with a +7.4 CPOE. That means he is completing them at a better rate than their difficulty predicts, not just getting lucky on volume. Watson's +0.507 EPA per target is the main beneficiary. Deep EPA is volatile on 27 attempts, but his career aDOT and aggressiveness have been stable around 8.5-8.9 and 16-17%, so the vertical identity is real even if the rate cools.

strengths.title: Under-center play-action efficiency
strengths.body: On 43 under-center plays he has +0.455 EPA with a 58.1% success rate and a 71.4% completion rate. Those numbers are far above his shotgun work. This is the LaFleur system doing what it is built to do, and it holds up as long as the coaching staff can keep him on schedule enough to call it.

strengths.title: Middle-of-field production
strengths.body: Throws between the numbers are returning +0.423 EPA and a 57.8% success rate, with four touchdowns. That is where Golden, Watson and Kraft win together. Two of his three interceptions also came there, so it is a high-reward lane rather than a risk-free one.

concerns.title: Accuracy has fallen off his 2025 level
concerns.body: A -2.05 CPOE and an 18.4% bad-throw rate are both bottom-tier, against an +5.5 CPOE and 12.5% bad-throw rate a year ago. The worst of it is front-loaded: 37.5% bad throws under heavy pressure in Week 1, then -13.6 CPOE at the Jets. Weeks 4-5 suggest it is correcting, so this reads more as a slump than a new baseline.

concerns.title: Long third downs with no run game
concerns.body: Green Bay's rushing EPA ranks 32nd of 32, which leaves him facing 8.2 yards to go on average on third down. He converts just 27.5% there, with a -9.0 CPOE. As long as the run game is this bad, and Chris Brooks is now on IR, he will keep facing these long-yardage downs.

concerns.title: Protection, now without the center
concerns.body: The offense is 30th in hit rate allowed, and he is hit or sacked on 19.4% of dropbacks. Starting center Jacob Monk (96% of snaps) is out, along with guard Aaron Banks. Interior protection is the piece most likely to worsen this week.

trend.note: His passing EPA went from -2.7 and -3.2 in the first two weeks to +6.9 at Tampa and +16.9 against Chicago. His CPOE flipped from deeply negative to +5.3 and +16.2 over the same stretch. The early weeks included the league's top-ranked defense and heavy pressure.

nextGame.headline: Worst pass defense in the league, if the wind cooperates
nextGame.body:
Dallas ranks 32nd in defensive EPA, 32nd in pass EPA allowed (+0.382) and 32nd in success rate. It is 29th in both sack rate and hit rate, so it rarely gets home. That removes the pressure that wrecked Love in Week 1. The Cowboys are also 32nd against short passes, which is the area where Love's accuracy has been weakest. That is a forgiving setup for a quarterback who needs easy completions to get back in rhythm. Opponents' top receivers are scoring 5.1 PPR over their averages and producing 0.69 EPA per target, which bodes well for Golden and Watson. Tight ends are getting 0.82 EPA per target, which bodes well for Kraft. Quarterbacks are averaging 21.5 PPR and 274 yards against them. One caveat is that offenses have been running more than usual against Dallas (-4.6 pass rate over norm). That partly reflects how good the Dallas offense has been. It ranks fourth in EPA, so this could become a shootout that forces volume.

Availability favors Green Bay's passing game. Dallas is without cornerbacks Cobie Durant and Joey Porter Jr. and linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, a thin unit losing coverage bodies. On Green Bay's side, losing center Monk and guard Banks is the real cost. Brooks on IR doesn't help a run game that was already failing, and Skyy Moore's possible absence matters little given his -0.291 EPA per target. The one real threat is weather. The forecast, 131 hours out, calls for 19 mph sustained wind with 39 mph gusts at an outdoor stadium. If that holds, it would cut into the deep shots that drive his efficiency. Treat it as a forecast, not a fact.

keyMatchups.title: Interior line vs a non-existent rush
keyMatchups.body: Green Bay is down its starting center, but Dallas generates hits on only 11.2% of dropbacks and sacks on 3.1%. A weak rush is the best possible opponent for a patched-up interior line. If Love gets clean pockets, his accuracy problems have mostly appeared under duress or on long third downs.

keyMatchups.title: Golden and Watson vs depleted corners
keyMatchups.body: Dallas allows 0.69 EPA per target to opposing WR1s, 30th in the league, and an explosive-pass rate that ranks 29th. With two corners out, Golden's volume (45 targets) and Watson's big-play efficiency both line up against the weakest point of the defense.

keyMatchups.title: Wind against the vertical game
keyMatchups.body: Love's deep game is his biggest edge, and 19 mph winds with heavy gusts would be the one thing that shuts it off. Dallas is 32nd against short throws, though, so even a wind-shortened plan has a soft target underneath.

nextGame.watch: Whether his early-down completion rate in shotgun looks like Weeks 4-5 or Weeks 1-3; that tells you if the accuracy slump is truly over.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect efficiency to drift up and volume to drift down. His career says he is a CPOE-positive passer, and the past two games point that way. The bottom-quartile accuracy should settle closer to neutral, lifting completion rate into the low-to-mid 60s. The yardage pace near 282 a game is padded by two blowout losses with 42 and 53 attempts. If Green Bay keeps winning, attempts settle closer to 30-35 and the yardage settles in the 240-280 range. The deep-ball EPA of +0.714 will regress on volume, but the vertical role is stable.

The touchdown rate of 5.4% is sustainable given his 2023-24 history, but the red-zone EPA is negative and his third-down conversion rate is poor. Seven red-zone touchdowns on 31 plays is efficient finishing that could cool. The run game is the structural ceiling on this offense. Without it, he lives in long-yardage passing situations, which caps his week-to-week consistency.
swingFactors: Whether the run game climbs off 32nd and keeps him out of long third downs
Health of the interior line with Monk and Banks out
Whether the Week 4-5 accuracy rebound holds

bets.reason: He has thrown exactly two touchdowns in all five games, including against two top-seven defenses. Dallas is last in pass EPA allowed and gives up two quarterback touchdowns a game. Red-zone throws are the least wind-sensitive part of his game.

Dallas allows 274 passing yards a game, is 32nd in pass EPA and short-pass EPA, rarely pressures, and is missing two corners. A 52.5 total implies a shootout against a top-four Dallas offense. The early wind forecast is the reason this isn't higher.

Green Bay gets the league's worst defense at home, and its own pass defense is second-best at limiting explosive passes. The Packers' 32nd-ranked run game and 26th-ranked run defense keep this a modest edge rather than a strong one.

confidence.note: Five-game sample with accuracy well off his career norm, an early and uncertain wind forecast, and two interior linemen out.
